root_cause.text: The netfilter ipset hash:* IPv4 range iteration loops in hash_ipmark4_uadt, hash_ipport4_uadt, hash_ipportip4_uadt, and hash_ipportnet4_uadt unconditionally increment a 32-bit IP iterator after processing the upper-bound address, causing the saved retry state (h->next) to advance past the requested range boundary.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes loops from `for (; ip <= ip_to; ip++)`/`ip++, i++` to manual end-of-loop increment with `if (ip == ip_to) break; ip++;`, and the commit/CVE text explicitly says “Advancing it once more can move the traversal state past the end of the request, so a later retry may continue from an unintended position.”

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full IPv4 range iteration and retry-state save logic in `hash_ipmark4_uadt()`, which is exactly where the described root cause occurs. The vulnerable construct is present: after `if (retried) ip = ntohl(h->next.ip);`, the loop is `for (; ip <= ip_to; ip++, i++) { ... }`, so `ip` is unconditionally incremented in the loop header even when processing the final element `ip == ip_to`. Because `e.ip = htonl(ip);` is set from the current iterator and the loop still uses unconditional `ip++` progression up to and past the upper bound, this commit contains the retry-state machinery implicated by the root cause, but it does not show any boundary-aware handling to prevent advancing saved state past the requested range end.
